items.q: How do you say 'I am eating bread' (some bread) in French?
items.random_wrong: Je mange le pain (which means 'the bread').
items.why: Students drop the partitive. French requires DU/DE LA/DES for 'some' even when English omits it. Skipping it makes the sentence ungrammatical in French.

items.q: What follows 'si' (if) in a conditional sentence like 'If I were rich, I would travel'?
items.correct: Imperfect tense (Si j'ÉTAIS riche, je voyagerais).
items.why: A classic error - students put conditional after si. The rule: si + IMPERFECT in the if-clause, conditional in the result clause. Never 'si je serais' - always 'si j'étais'.
Students assume librairie = library. It actually means BOOKSHOP. The French word for library is bibliothèque. Both relate to books but serve different purposes.

items.q: In which year did Algeria gain independence from France?
items.why: The answer examiners want is: 1962. “1954” is the distractor this question was built around — if it tempted you, that's the exact gap to close.

items.q: Which is NOT part of the Maghreb?
items.why: It's Sénégal. “Algérie” is the classic near-miss here; knowing why it's wrong is worth as much as knowing the right answer.

items.q: In what year was Quebec's Law 101 (Charter of the French Language) passed?
items.why: The real figure is 1977. The wrong options cluster deliberately close — anchor the exact number to one concrete fact so it can't drift.
